title: Watch the Fire from Afar

source.chapter: Watch the Fire from Across the River
source.quote: When their order breaks down in the open, wait quietly for them to turn on each other; the violent and reckless bring ruin on themselves.

moral: Some things you do not rush to step into — wait until they fall apart on their own.

story.title: A Quarrel Across the River
story.text: Two brothers on the far bank started quarrelling — you could hear it across the river.
story.narration: Cao Cao brought his soldiers to the river. On the far bank were two brothers, and they fell out with each other first — you could hear it across the water.

story.title: He Sat Still
story.text: Cao Cao sat still on the bank and watched the far side scatter on its own.
story.narration: Cao Cao sat on his own bank and never crossed the river. Before long the two brothers and their people drifted apart — one river, and nobody had crossed it.

keyMoment.question: They are quarrelling across the river. Do you go over and break it up?

options.text: Cross the river and break it up at once
options.hint: The moment you step in, the two of them turn on you together.

options.text: Do not cross — wait and watch

options.hint: Step in, and they will deal with you first.

keyMoment.reveal: Some things you do not rush to step into — wait until they fall apart on their own.

misconceptions: If people are quarrelling, you should rush in and break it up
Watching from the far bank means enjoying the show while a friend is in trouble

quiz.question: What did Cao Cao do while they quarrelled across the river?
options: He sat on the bank and waited; he did not cross
He crossed the river at once to break it up
He sent soldiers over to help
quiz.explanation: Cao Cao sat still on his own bank and waited for them to fall apart — and they scattered by themselves.

quiz.question: What does the Thirty-Six Stratagems say to do?
options: When their order breaks down in the open, wait quietly for them to turn on each other
Cross over and pull them apart first
Use the confusion to grab things
quiz.explanation: Their order breaks down in the open while you wait quietly — you do not rush to move.

quiz.question: Two classmates start quarrelling. When is the best time to step in?
options: After they have said their piece and cooled down
quiz.explanation: If you step in at once, both of them will blame you — wait until they have finished and cooled down, then speak.

temptations.line: The moment you cross, the two of them turn on you together
The moment you cross, the two of them turn on you together

lines: Sit and watch for a while. There is no hurry.
This quarrel is theirs to settle.
Let them fall apart, and the far bank goes quiet.
